title: Atomic Fences and Total Order
goal: Decouple synchronization from variables and understand sequential consistency.

sections.text: In C++ and Java, memory fences synchronize non-atomic operations across threads. Rust provides `fence` to decouple memory synchronization from atomic variables.

sections.caption: Release fence prevents preceding writes from moving down.

sections.text: A `Release` fence paired with an `Acquire` fence in another thread establishes a synchronization barrier.
In contrast, `Ordering::SeqCst` enforces a single globally agreed ordering of atomic operations across all threads.

sections.caption: SeqCst enforces a global total order across threads.

sections.text: `Ordering::SeqCst` is the safest default, but incurs extra instruction overhead on weak memory hardware like ARM.

explanation: Decouple synchronization from variables and understand sequential consistency.
